title: West Midlands Pantomime & Festive Season 2026: The Ultimate Family Guide
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: From high-flying adventures in Neverland to slapstick classics across Birmingham, Wolverhampton, Lichfield, Stafford, and Coventry, explore the top family pantomimes and festive stage productions lighting up the Midlands this winter.
bodyHtml:
Festive Magic Across the Midlands

As autumn draws in, theatres across the West Midlands are preparing for the loudest, sparkliest, and most joyous time of the theatrical calendar. Whether your family thrives on classic dame banter, slapstick comedy, or spectacular scenic transformations, the 2026 festive season offers an extraordinary range of accessible, family-focused productions.

For neurodivergent families and sensory-sensitive theatregoers, navigating the high-energy world of pantomime often requires careful planning. Fortunately, venues across our region are continuing to raise the bar with comprehensive access schedules, dedicated breakout spaces, and tailored sensory adjustments.

Slapstick Royalty: The Big Stage Pantomimes

Sleeping Beauty at Birmingham Hippodrome

The Hippodrome panto remains an undisputed Midlands institution. This year, Birmingham pantomime legends Matt Slack and Andrew Ryan return to anchor Sleeping Beauty. Audiences can expect lavish sets, high-octane physical comedy, and show-stopping musical numbers. With a dedicated Relaxed Performance scheduled for late January alongside BSL, Captioned, and Audio Described dates, the Hippodrome ensures everyone can join in the festive cheer. A firm family favouritie at BTMC, Matt Slack has won us over time and again and we've witnessed first hand his "show must go on" approach, which makes even the cast howl with laughter. We can't wait to see what's in store this year! 

Treasure Island at Wolverhampton Grand Theatre

Fresh from clinching Best Panto in the UK at the UK Pantomime Awards, Wolverhampton Grand sets sail with a brand-new swashbuckling title: Treasure Island. Audience favourites Ian Adams and Tam Ryan team up once again for an original high-seas adventure. The Grand continues its stellar reputation for accessibility, programming three daytime relaxed performances featuring lowered sound volume, softened lighting cues, and calm breakout rooms. The lovable Tam Ryan has had us cry with laughter over the years, oh yes he has! We can't wait to see his swashbuckling adventure for 2026!

Beauty and the Beast at Belgrade Theatre, Coventry

Coventry’s favourite dame, Iain Lauchlan, returns to write and star in Beauty and the Beast. Known for brilliant local wit, eye-popping costumes, and family warmth, the Belgrade offers an exceptionally inclusive run—welcoming all ages with babes-in-arms lap tickets, booster seats, touch tours, and combined captioned/relaxed performances.

Robin Hood at Lichfield Garrick

The Lichfield Garrick is transforming into Sherwood Forest this winter as it prepares to stage Robin Hood. Marking the venue's first in-house-produced pantomime in over a decade, the festive spectacular arrives straight from the Garrick family to yours following a stellar milestone year that saw the venue produce its hit in-house musical Disenchanted! and secure its long-term future through an extended council lease.

We love a home-grown festive treat here at Behind the Magic Curtain, and the 2026 line-up promises double the laughter, double the fun, and double the Ben! Garrick veteran Ben Thornton takes on the titular role of Robin Hood, joined by Great British Pantomime Award winner Ben Stock, who is ready to delight family audiences as the iconic Nurse Nellie. They are joined by Joe Feeney as the dastardly Sheriff of Nottingham, this production is set to be an unmissable festive highlight packed with traditional cheer, live music, and magical panto mischief.

Aladdin at Stafford Gatehouse Theatre

Over at Stafford Gatehouse, families can take flight on a magic carpet with Aladdin, starring Mark Rhodes, David Phipps-Davis, and Samantha Spragg. Packed with lively song-and-dance numbers, vibrant villains, and side-splitting physical comedy, the production features relaxed and signed performances in late December.

The Gentle Magic Alternative: Peter Pan at The Rep

While traditional pantomimes bring undeniable glitter and boisterous call-and-response fun, the shouting, strobe effects, and pyrotechnics can be sensory overload for many children. If your family is looking for genuine festive wonder and theatrical spectacle without the deafening "Behind you!" chaos, Peter Pan at Birmingham Rep is the standout festive alternative.

Adapted by Phil Porter with an original score by Ruth Chan and directed by Joe Murphy, this faithful stage production of J.M. Barrie’s classic tale delivers breathless flying sequences, imaginative storytelling, and pirate mischief. It provides all the festive warmth and escapism of a seasonal outing within the gentler, immersive structure of a classic family play. The Rep backs this up with an exemplary access programme, including relaxed staging, touch tours, and captioned shows.

title: Magical Firsts: The Best Early Years Festive Shows in the West Midlands for 2026
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: Looking for the perfect first theatre experience this Christmas? We've rounded up the most magical, sensory-friendly, and bite-sized festive adventures arriving in the West Midlands for toddlers and young children in 2026.
bodyHtml:
Gentle Magic for Little Ones

When it comes to introducing toddlers and young children to live theatre, the festive season is the absolute perfect time. While traditional, loud pantomimes can sometimes be a bit overwhelming for early years and neurodivergent children, the West Midlands has some incredibly thoughtfully designed, bite-sized shows arriving this winter. As parents, finding that balance of sensory-friendly lighting, gentle pacing, and a forgiving running time is essential—and this year’s line-up completely delivers.

One Tiny Penguin (Birmingham Hippodrome) 

If you’ve been following our family's theatre adventures, you will know exactly how much James, Charlotte, and I adored the Hippodrome's previous 'My First Musical' productions. This year, the series continues with One Tiny Penguin. Starring Dylan Collymore, this 60-minute adventure follows Lumi the penguin as he travels the world to discover what it truly means to be brave. It’s tailor-made for toddlers, highly sensory-aware, and packed with catchy songs that you'll undoubtedly be singing well into the new year!

Father Christmas (Belgrade Theatre, Coventry)

Over at the Belgrade Theatre, the Olivier Award-nominated Pins & Needles Productions are bringing back a true festive favourite: Father Christmas. Based on Raymond Briggs’ much-loved book, this highly visual, 50-minute stage adaptation gives young audiences a delightful peek into Santa’s busiest day of the year. With a gentle pace and visually engaging puppetry, it is the ideal first-time theatre experience for children under 6.

The Gingerbread Boy (Stafford Gatehouse Theatre)

For a fresh, sweet treat, Stafford Gatehouse is hosting The Gingerbread Boy for a strictly limited run in mid-December. Deep in Fairy-tale Forest, a remarkable boy made entirely of gingerbread embarks on a madcap journey of discovery alongside his new friend Blake. With a running time of just 50 minutes and a surprise Christmas Eve visitor, this story about friendship and celebrating differences is a beautiful festive introduction. Plus, every child's ticket includes a free present!

title: Affordable Children's Shows Heading to Stafford Gatehouse
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: Looking for pocket-friendly family theatre this autumn and winter? Stafford Gatehouse Theatre has lined up four brilliant, low-stress productions packed with music, magic, and meet-and-greets.
bodyHtml:
Finding high-quality, memorable live theatre that does not stretch the family budget can feel like quite a challenge, especially as autumn half term and the festive rush approach. Stafford Gatehouse Theatre has put together a cracking line-up of accessible, heartwarming, and delightfully interactive family productions for the remainder of 2026—making stage trips simple, engaging, and cost-friendly for all ages.

Whether introducing a toddler to their very first auditorium experience or bringing primary schoolers along for gentle spooky fun and winter wonderland adventures, these four productions make brilliant entry points into live performance.

Early Years Interactive Fun: Spot’s Birthday Party

Kicking off during the October half-term break on October 24, Eric Hill's classic storybook puppy bounds onto the Gatehouse stage. Tailored for ages 2 and up, Spot’s Birthday Party features clear, integrated Makaton, infectious sing-along tunes, and gentle interactive party games alongside Steve the Monkey, Tom the Crocodile, and Helen the Hippo.

Ages 2+ Sensory Friendly 

Even better for young theatregoers: every single ticket includes a free party hat plus a post-show meet-and-greet with Spot himself, offering great value and reassuring pacing for neurodivergent little ones who love tactile, predictable storytelling.

Spots Birthday Party 

Gentle Halloween Thrills: The Spooky Magic Show

If you want festive Halloween entertainment without the sensory overload or frightening jump scares, The Spooky Magic Show on October 31st hits the sweet spot. When Rufus the Dog mistakes Uncle Cadabra’s wand for a bone and hides it up in the attic, apprentice sorcerer Sam needs young audience helpers to craft the counter-spell.

With colourful stage illusions, lovable puppets, and lots of audience participation, this is an uplifting, giggly show designed specifically for families with kids aged 4 and older.

Ages 4+ 

The Spooky Magic Show 

Chilly Half-Term Pantomime Vibes: Freezin’

Arriving right after Halloween on November 1, Freezin’ brings classic fairytale chaos and high-energy laughs. When Jack Frost blankets the kingdom in eternal ice, Princess Honour joins forces with the wonderfully ridiculous Silly Snowy to break the frost spell and help Queen Ellie navigate her icy powers.

Brimming with bright musical numbers, eye-catching costumes, and silly comedy that invites plenty of enthusiastic booing and cheering, it delivers all the festive spirit of pantomime season at an affordable family ticket price.

Freezin 

Cosy Christmas Storytelling: The Gingerbread Boy

Rounding out the season on December 12 and 13, The Gingerbread Boy brings warm festive magic to the Gatehouse. Following young Blake’s discovery of a magical cookie cottage in Fairy-tale Forest, this sweet tale celebrates friendship, kindness, and embracing what makes each of us unique, Heartwarming!

Ages 3+ 

Running at a gentle, attention-friendly 50 minutes, it is ideal for ages 3+. To top off the festive cheer, Santa makes a special surprise appearance after the performance—and every child ticket includes a free gift to take home!

The Gingerbread Boy

title: Birmingham Rep Announces Full Casting for Peter Pan
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: Birmingham Rep has revealed the full cast for its festive production of Peter Pan, featuring Iverson Yabut as Peter and original music by Ruth Chan.
bodyHtml:
Birmingham Rep has announced full casting for its forthcoming festive production of Peter Pan, J M Barrie’s much-loved children’s story, which runs between Wednesday 18 November 2026 and Sunday 17 January 2027.

This new production is adapted by Phil Porter, featuring over 20 original songs by composer Ruth Chan. Directed by The Rep’s Artistic Director, Joe Murphy, the show promises a faithful late Victorian/Edwardian setting alongside genuine flying, intricate puppetry, and a fresh coming-of-age journey for Wendy.

The cast features Iverson Yabut (A Christmas Carol: A Ghost Story) as Peter Pan, Amber Sylvia Edwards as Wendy, and Hannah McPake taking on the dual roles of Captain Hook and Mrs Darling. They are joined by Emmy Stonelake as Tinker Bell, Jack Benjamin as Mr Darling/Skylights, and a talented ensemble portraying the Darling children, pirates, and Lost Boys.

title: Fabric Announces Autumn Season for THIS IS DANCE in Birmingham
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: Fabric’s THIS IS DANCE partnership returns to Birmingham this autumn, bringing together exceptional local and international dance talent across multiple city venues.
bodyHtml:
Fabric, a strategic dance development organisation based in the Midlands, is delighted to announce incredible performances this autumn, presented as part of THIS IS DANCE.

Now in its second year, THIS IS DANCE is a unique partnership which includes Fabric, Birmingham Hippodrome, Birmingham Repertory Theatre, Birmingham Royal Ballet, Midlands Arts Centre, Fierce Festival and Sampad Arts. The partners share an ambition to create more opportunity, supporting artists, and increasing engagement, making dance a vital part of Birmingham’s cultural identity.

With performances from 13 October through to 26 November, the latest programme brings together a local and international line-up of artists and companies from the UK, Italy, USA, Canada, Poland, the Netherlands, Germany and Benin. Fabric is also offering co-presented performances throughout the autumn season.

title: Birmingham Rep’s: A Thousand Splendid Suns to Tour in 2027
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: Following a sell-out run in 2025, Birmingham Rep has announced that its acclaimed production of Khaled Hosseini’s A Thousand Splendid Suns will embark on a major UK national tour in Spring 2027, opening at Birmingham Rep on 29 January.
bodyHtml:
Following a sell-out run in 2025, Birmingham Rep is pleased to announce that its acclaimed production of A Thousand Splendid Suns will embark on a national tour in Spring 2027, beginning at Birmingham Rep from 29 January.

Based on the international best-selling novel by Khaled Hosseini—which has sold over 38 million copies—and adapted for the stage by Ursula Rani Sarma, A Thousand Splendid Suns is directed by Kimberley Sykes. The powerful production features Rina Fatania making a welcome return to reprise her role as Mariam, with Set and Costume Design by Simon Kenny. Set in a war-torn 1992 Afghanistan, the play tells the unflinching story of survival, resilience, and the strength of the human spirit as two women, Laila and Mariam, become unlikely allies amidst starvation, brutality, and fear.

Ages 14+  Mature Themes 

Kimberley Sykes shared: “It’s an honour to be asked to direct this courageous and vital piece of storytelling. Ursula’s adaptation of Khaled Hosseini’s seismic novel burns with defiance and soothes with humanity. Now, five years into the Taliban’s current rule and women’s rights in Afghanistan at crisis point, this play seems more urgent than ever.”

Joe Murphy, Artistic Director at Birmingham Rep, added: “A Thousand Splendid Suns played to packed houses here in Birmingham in 2025, and I’m thrilled and proud that The Rep is taking this deeply affecting piece of theatre on the road as part of a national tour in 2027.”

Photo credit: A Thousand Splendid Suns. Production Images from 2025 production. Photos by Ellie Kurttz

title: Rehearsal Images Released for Sylvia: A Musical Revolution UK Tour and Royal Albert Hall Run
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: First-look rehearsal photos are here for the return of the Olivier-nominated hip-hop, funk and soul musical Sylvia, starring Beverley Knight and Naomi Katiyo ahead of its UK tour and historic Royal Albert Hall residency.
bodyHtml:
First-look rehearsal photographs have been revealed for the triumphant return of Sylvia: A Musical Revolution. The Olivier-nominated production is gearing up for a limited UK tour this Autumn, culminating in a landmark five-performance run at the iconic Royal Albert Hall from 13th to 15th November 2026.

We are massive champions of powerhouse theatre here at Behind the Magic Curtain, and seeing the phenomenal Beverley Knight MBE step back into her Olivier Award-winning role as Emmeline Pankhurst alongside Naomi Katiyo as Sylvia Pankhurst is nothing short of thrilling. Created by ZooNation's visionary Kate Prince alongside writers Priya Parmar, Josh Cohen, and DJ Walde, this production fuses electrifying hip-hop, funk, and soul to bring the untold story of the rebellious middle child of the Pankhurst family vibrantly to life.

This autumn's run carries incredible historical resonance. The Royal Albert Hall served as the backdrop for nearly thirty suffragette events between 1908 and 1913, affectionately known to the movement as a 'Temple of Liberty' before the Suffragettes were famously barred in April 1913. Returning to the venue feels like the ultimate circle-of-life celebration. Even better for family audiences and young theatregoers, the production will host the UK's largest-ever education matinee on Friday 13th November in partnership with Go Live Theatre and The Garek Trust, welcoming nearly 5,000 children and young people with tickets priced at just £10 to ensure live theatre remains accessible to all.

title: Stage Magic on Your Doorstep: Creative Burntwood Project Unveils Jam-Packed Year Two Season
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: From interactive Shakespeare and pyjama Halloween parties to £5 baby sensory music and festive Dickensian classics, Lichfield Garrick’s Creative Burntwood project unveils an action-packed new season for families and local theatregoers.
bodyHtml:
Bringing the arts directly into the heart of our local communities is where real stage magic begins. Now heading into its second exciting year, the Creative Burntwood project—led by the Lichfield Garrick Theatre in partnership with Burntwood Town Council and Lichfield District Council—is continuing its mission to enrich local culture, enliven neighbourhood venues, and make live performance welcoming and accessible to all.

Supported by Arts Council England’s Place Partnership Fund, the outreach initiative follows an incredible first year featuring social media sensation Jonny Cole, top-tier comedy from Manford’s Comedy Club, and high-flying children's circus shows.

This autumn and winter, the project returns with an even richer programme crafted especially for curious young minds, growing families, and relaxed community outings.

Younger theatregoers can kick off the new school year on 20th September with Magical Honey at Chase Terrace Community Centre—a spellbinding blend of South Asian dance, live music, and cultural storytelling celebrating the triumph of art over adversity (Ages 5+). Creative hands will love MakeBeth at Ashmole Bowls & Social Club on 11th October, where Shakespeare's classic is reinvented through interactive cardboard crafting (Ages 7+).

For Halloween, slip on your cosy sleepwear for The Witch Who Couldn't Sleep at Burntwood Memorial Institute on 25th October—a sensory-friendly, interactive pyjama party blending animation, atmospheric lighting, and call-and-response storytelling where children guide the plot (Ages 3+).

The family programme stretches well into 2027 with non-verbal bunraku puppetry in Secrets of the Selkie Sea (16th January, Ages 6+) and puppet encounters in The Zoo that Comes to You at Burntwood Library (7th April, Ages 5+). Finding budget-friendly sensory adventures for tiny tots can often be tough, but Babies Adventures in Music brings an inspiring, accessible sensory session to Burntwood Memorial Institute on 15th March for just £5 (Ages 0–18 months).

Grown-ups are equally well catered for with the return of Manford’s Comedy Club (26th September), BBC Radio 2 Folk Award winners Kathryn Roberts & Sean Lakeman (7th October), and spine-lingering ghost stories in Tales After Dark at Burntwood Library (18th March).

When the festive season arrives, experience a Dickensian classic staged in the atmospheric setting of St Anne’s Church with A Christmas Carol (4th December, complete with optional mince pies and mulled wine), or join Father Christmas’ reindeer caretaker in A Christmas Story at Ashmole Bowls & Social Club (12th December) for an uplifting journey about communication, empathy, and festive cheer.

title: Birmingham Royal Ballet Cygnets Take to the Water Ahead of Swan Lake at Birmingham Hippodrome
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: Birmingham Royal Ballet’s cygnets made a splash at Cannon Hill Park’s boating lake to celebrate Sir Peter Wright’s Swan Lake heading to Birmingham Hippodrome and London's Sadler's Wells this autumn.
bodyHtml:
Dancers from Birmingham Royal Ballet made a splash at Cannon Hill Park’s boating lake this week, striking a pose alongside the iconic swan boats to celebrate the upcoming revival of Sir Peter Wright and Galina Samsova’s world-renowned production of Swan Lake.

The company’s first cast of four cygnets — Rachele Pizzillo, Reina Fuchigami, Rosanna Ely, and Sofia Liñares — took time out of intensive rehearsals to visit the historic Birmingham park, posing on the water before taking to the stage at Birmingham Hippodrome from Wednesday 23 September to Saturday 3 October 2026.

The cygnets in Swan Lake perform the iconic Danse des petits cygnes (Dance of the Little Swans) in Act II — one of the most recognisable and demanding pieces of classical choreography in ballet. The four dancers must cross arms in unbroken formation and move in precise, flawless unison, capturing young cygnets huddling together.

Set to Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky’s legendary score performed live by the Royal Ballet Sinfonia, the ballet tells the timeless story of Prince Siegfried and Odette, a princess cursed by the sorcerer Baron von Rothbart to live as a swan by day and a woman by night.

Birmingham & London Ages 5+ Live Orchestra

Following its ten-day run at Birmingham Hippodrome, the production will transfer to London’s Sadler’s Wells Theatre from Wednesday 28 to Saturday 31 October 2026.

Families looking to get a closer look at the world of classical ballet can also catch Birmingham Royal Ballet in the city centre this weekend as part of Birmingham Weekender in the Bullring on Saturday 29 August, featuring free Swan Lake children's dance workshops.

title: Sweeney Todd Smashes Box Office Records at Birmingham Rep
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: Stephen Sondheim’s musical masterpiece Sweeney Todd has become the most successful musical production in Birmingham Rep's history, taking nearly £1.4 million at the box office.
bodyHtml:
The Birmingham Rep is celebrating a monumental achievement as its critically acclaimed, 5-star production of Stephen Sondheim’s musical masterpiece, Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street, officially became the theatre’s most successful musical production in history.

Playing to an impressive 82% capacity across its six-week run—which concluded on August 15th—the landmark production sold 31,283 tickets and grossed nearly £1.4 million at the box office.

MATURE THEMES  

The dark, razor-sharp musical captured international attention, welcoming theatregoers from 53 different countries. The production also built an exceptionally dedicated following closer to home: 430 audience members returned to see the show more than once, with one super-fan attending an astonishing nineteen times.

Garnering more than twenty 5-star reviews from national and regional critics, the production featured a powerhouse cast led by West End and Broadway sensation Ramin Karimloo in the title role, Olivier Award-nominee and cabaret icon Meow Meow as Mrs Lovett, and three-time Olivier Award-winner David Bedella as Judge Turpin.

Proudly produced and crafted entirely in the West Midlands, the show's entire staging—from the intricate sets to the bespoke costumes and props—was built by The Rep’s in-house team of artisans and rehearsed on site.

The Rep’s Artistic Director, Joe Murphy, reflected on the milestone:

“When I decided to include Sweeney Todd in my first season here at The Rep I could never have imagined the reception it would get. That success is down to everyone who helped bring it to the stage, from the extraordinary company—led by Ramin, Meow and David—to the amazing creative team, and everyone at The Rep who works behind the scenes.

“I’m deeply proud that the show was made here in Birmingham. Everything, from the set, costumes and props, was created by our wonderfully talented craftspeople. And we rehearsed the production here too. I think that led to something really special.

“It’s brilliant that the show has been so popular, attracting people from across the globe to come to The Rep and Birmingham. Audiences truly took Sweeney to their hearts, and I’ve loved seeing how they responded to it with so much enthusiasm and delight.”
detailsHtml:
• Production: Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street 
  • Venue: The Birmingham Rep (Main Stage) 
  • Run: Ended 15 August 
  • Box Office Milestone: Over 31,000 tickets sold & £1.4M grossed 
  • Starring: Ramin Karimloo, Meow Meow, David Bedella 
  • Direction: Joe Murphy

title: London Theatre Week Is Back: It’s Like Christmas Come Early for Theatre Fans!
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: London Theatre Week has officially returned with exclusive West End ticket offers from just £15, £25, and £35! Discover incredible savings across more than 80 major productions, including family favourites like The Lion King, Oliver!, and Wicked.
bodyHtml:
If your household loves the buzz of live theatre as much as ours does, consider this the ultimate treat: Special Promotion — London Theatre Week has arrived, and it truly feels like Christmas come early!

The West End’s biggest ticket promotion of the season is officially live, opening up access to more than 80 world-class shows with exclusive, set promotional pricing from just £15, £25, and £35. Whether you’re looking to introduce your little ones to their very first big musical, secure brilliant seats for an autumn weekend getaway, or lock in half-term and festive treats well before the rush, this is the single best time of the year to grab incredible bargains.

Our Personal Family Favourites Included

What makes this year’s London Theatre Week lineup especially magical is that some of our absolute all-time family favourites are included in the exclusive pricing tiers:

  • The Lion King (Lyceum Theatre): Pure theatrical magic from the very first opening call of the Circle of Life. Julie Taymor’s breathtaking puppetry and visual grandeur make it an unforgettable sensory spectacle for kids of all ages.

  • Oliver! (Gielgud Theatre): Lionel Bart’s classic masterpiece is back in London, packed with timeless tunes, irresistible energy, and rich storytelling that captivates every generation.

Ticket allocations at these fixed price bands are limited and sell fast, so be sure to check dates and book early!

title: A New Stage Begins: Behind The Magic Curtain Officially Relaunches
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: We are proud to unveil the brand-new Behind The Magic Curtain — rebuilt from the ground up to bring UK families detailed neurodivergent theatre guides, sensory ratings, and West End touring insights.
bodyHtml:
When my son turned to me in tears after his very first show in 2019 and whispered, "Mummy, please go behind the magic curtain and ask them to come back and see me," a spark was ignited. Over the years, as our family learned to navigate ADHD, sensory overstimulation, and an enduring passion for live performance, that spark grew into Behind The Magic Curtain.

Today, we are thrilled to raise the curtain on our completely relaunched website. We have redesigned every part of the platform to remove the guesswork, stress, and anxiety from planning family theatre visits and immersive days out.

Here is what you will find across the new platform:

  • Sensory Strategies — In-depth parent insights covering sudden sound spikes, lighting effects, queue management, and quiet break spaces for all featured productions.

  • What's On & UK Tours — Up-to-date tracking of West End transfers, regional Midlands venues, and accessible relaxed performances.

  • Venue Accessibility Directory — Step-free access audits, hearing loops, and sensory breakout spaces across regional theatres.

Live theatre has the power to inspire every child. Our mission is to ensure every family feels confident walking through the foyer doors, finding their seats, and experiencing the wonder together.

Take a look around the new site, test out the interactive guides, and join our community newsletter below to stay updated on all upcoming productions and relaxed performances.

Katy x
